subject: Transient GPU burst: billing credit proposal & VAT handling (CloudBridge)
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@cloudbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term GPU burst & how you will invoice/VAT the delta

Jordan —

We ran a one-off capacity spike last week for a training job and consumed ~320 GPU-hours beyond our committed pool (10x 32-core GPUs, ~3 days). We were charged for the overage but our procurement team is asking whether Redwood can treat this as a temporary burst (we expected it to be covered by a short-term top-up) and either:

- apply a one-time credit for the unused portion of the reserved pool we didn’t use this month, OR
- reclassify the excess as a separate transient charge with a pro-rated invoice so our finance can match costs to the project.

Two specific asks:
1) Can you confirm how you’d calculate a pro-rata amount for a mid-cycle burst and whether VAT will be applied to the credit reversal or invoice adjustment?
2) Our AP team needs an amended invoice (with PO# 987543) and a VAT document for our EU legal entity — we can share the VAT registration.

I’ve attached a short usage export and our internal PO stub. Appreciate a quick path here; procurement needs to close the month.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Sr. Cloud Ops Manager
CloudBridge Systems
Attachments: Usage_export-Jun01-07.csv (usage summary); PO_987543.pdf (procurement PO)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term GPU burst & how you will invoice/VAT the delta

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the note and the files. Short version: yes, we can do a one-time reconciliation that both (a) issues a credit for the portion of your committed capacity that went unused during the same billing month and (b) produces a standalone transient-charge invoice for the extra GPU-hours.

How we’ll handle VAT and credits:
- Credits: processed as a negative line on a revised invoice; VAT is adjusted according to the tax treatment on the original charge and the customer VAT registration you provide.
- Transient charge: issued as a separate invoice for the actual overage; VAT applied per your VAT status/region.

I’ve looped in Marcus (billing) and Monica (finance) to confirm the exact proration math and to draft the revised invoice + credit that matches your PO. I’ll aim to get a draft back by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps for us:
1) Marcus to validate the usage CSV and produce the delta calculation.
2) Monica to confirm whether we can put the credit against your July invoice or issue a refund (you prefer credit application).
3) Alex — please send your VAT registration PDF and the final PO number (I see PO_987543 but confirm).

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudBridge burst — calc & credit recommendation

Marcus / Monica — forwarding Alex’s request (below) and the usage CSV. Quick notes:

On Mon, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700, Alex Morgan <alex@cloudbridge.com> wrote:
> Jordan —
> 
> We ran a one-off capacity spike last week for a training job and consumed ~320 GPU-hours beyond our committed pool ...

Prelim numbers (from looking at the CSV):
- Committed pool: 720 GPU-hours/month (10 GPUs * 72 hours equivalent for the period).
- Actual usage: 1,040 GPU-hours for the month window Alex supplied.
- Overage: 320 GPU-hours.

Billing options (recommendation inline):
A) One-time credit for "unused reserved pool portion" — compute unused reserved hours = max(0, committed - baseline project usage). This is messy because the reserved pool is shared. We can offer a one-time goodwill credit equal to the estimated unused portion: recommended credit = (estimated unused hours / committed hours) * monthly commitment fee.

B) Separate transient-charge invoice for the 320 GPU-hours at on-demand rate. Pros: clean matching on CloudBridge accounting. Cons: might be higher unit price.

Recommendation: Combine both — issue the transient-charge invoice for the 320 GPU-hours and apply a one-time adjustment credit equal to the estimated unused share (capped at total monthly commitment). This preserves revenue recognition and satisfies procurement's matching needs.

Action items:
- Marcus: run exact per-hour proration and produce a delta spreadsheet (include tax calculations per entity).
- Monica: confirm credit application flow (apply to July invoice vs. refund) and any AR/collection implications.

Marcus / Monica, please prioritize — procurement needs an amended invoice they can file this week.

Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@cloudbridge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term GPU burst & how you will invoice/VAT the delta

Alex / Jordan —

I ran the numbers and attached a short workbook (Burst_Capacity_Invoice_Delta.xlsx). Key points:
- On-demand rate applied to overage: $6.50 / GPU-hour.
- Transient charge for 320 GPU-hours = $2,080.00 (net).
- Estimated unused committed hours (based on average non-spike usage): 140 GPU-hours -> credit equivalent = (140 / 720) * monthly commitment fee. For CloudBridge your monthly commitment fee = $14,400 -> credit = $2,800.

Net effect if we apply the recommendation (transient invoice + credit):
- Transient invoice: +$2,080.00 (separate invoice).
- One-time credit: -$2,800.00 (negative line on revised invoice).
- Net position: credit larger than the transient-invoice amount = customer-facing net credit of $720.00 to be applied to next invoice or refunded.

VAT/tax treatment:
- The transient invoice will have VAT applied per CloudBridge legal entity. Alex: provide VAT registration and entity country.
- The credit: we will issue a revised invoice that shows a negative line; VAT adjusted proportionally. If the credit sits as a future credit (applied to July invoice), the VAT on the credit will be documented on the July invoice as well.

Monica: please confirm whether to (A) apply the $720 net credit to July invoice, or (B) issue a refund to the original payment method.

Alex: attached workbook and a proposed wording for the amended invoice description to satisfy procurement.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Burst_Capacity_Invoice_Delta.xlsx

From: Alex Morgan <alex@cloudbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@cloudbridge.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00

Jordan / Marcus —

Thanks for the fast turnaround — the delta workbook looks good and the combined approach is acceptable.

We confirm: PO# 987543. Attached is our VAT registration for CloudBridge EU entity (VAT-ID: EU12345678). Please issue:
1) Transient overage invoice for $2,080 (apply VAT per EU registration).
2) Revised invoice showing the $2,800 credit and the resulting net credit of $720 to be applied to the July 2026 invoice.

Procurement requests the amended invoice PDF and the separate transient invoice by EOB tomorrow if possible — they need it for the month close. If you’re going to require a signature for a subscription amendment to memorialize the transient burst policy, send the DocuSign link and we’ll sign quickly.

Alex Morgan
